key_insight: A recursive deep learning pipeline can replace slow finite-element simulation to predict the full transverse-compression response of synthetic plant fibers and estimate their Young's modulus.
engineering_relevance: This enables rapid, high-throughput mechanical screening of natural-fiber geometries, supporting faster design of plant-fiber-reinforced composites.
method: Generate 1,000 synthetic hemp fiber cross-sections, with and without lumen, and use FE simulations as ground truth.
Use two coupled recursive U-Nets to predict stepwise deformation and internal stress-field evolution under transverse compression.
Feed the final stress field into a regression CNN to estimate transverse Young's modulus.
evidence_signal: On the test set, the model achieved SSIM 0.9574 ± 0.0074, RMSE 0.0345 ± 0.0079, and modulus prediction performance of R² 0.938 ± 0.024 with MAE 24.31 ± 1.23 MPa and MAPE 5.25 ± 0.91%.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on synthetic geometries derived from real hemp cross-sections, so generalization to other fiber species, loading conditions, or manufacturing defects may require retraining or validation.
paper_title: Deep Learning-based Mechanical Characterization of Synthetically Generated Plant Fibers under Transverse Compression
